subject: Record the owner's decisions on the Loom refinement questions
description:
All decided 2026-10-03. Items 1–4 were delegated by the owner ("Determine optimal / recommended – coherent and cohesive approach"), and item 9 follows the same delegation as a reversible in-repository engineering choice. Items from 10 on are implementation conflicts resolved under the task 1 conflict rule.

1. Workspace naming.
   - Every stored-state operation takes `workspaceId`. `--workspace` is a discovery hint only.
   - Inline-model mode is an explicit alternative that is not trusted, and is never mixed with a handle.
   - Single-workspace writes carry MutationExpectation {model, config, policy, imports}. Cross-model plan, apply and publish carry `expectedVector`.
   - No `expectedRevision` string, no shim, no "restart the server" refusal.
2. Outcome vocabulary. One status system.
   - CheckResult stays PASS|FAIL|UNKNOWN|NOT_APPLICABLE: passed→PASS; failed→FAIL; unavailable→UNKNOWN with a typed cause naming the missing dependency; cancelled→UNKNOWN with cause `cancelled`.
   - At run level there are testOutcome, cleanup.state and a lifecycle outcome. Success = required checks PASS and cleanup clean.
   - A requested versus completed cancellation is a run phase.
3. Nesting.
   - One `.loom` per repository root; init stays root-only.
   - Members are repositories inside the parent's tree, addressed by repositoryPath. An outside system is consumed as a published bundle.
   - Per child, either undelegated (the parent claims its roots) or delegated (a listed member with an implementation .loom).
   - An unlisted child .loom under a parent claim is SCOPE_OVERLAP.
4. Model records, added within format 1 (fields in task 7, rules in task 30):
   (a) explicit terminal states, with dead-end, terminal-with-exit and unreachable-state rules;
   (b) TrustBoundary.within, with a cycle rule;
   (c) ordered Workflow.steps (actor component, action operation|mutation|routine, target, failure handling retry|compensate with its reference|abort; trust crossings derived from deployment units), plus a sequence diagram kind.
5. A loom-worker agent definition (general-purpose without the Agent tool), created in task 33.
6. Machine setup:
   6a. Pester for Windows PowerShell 5.1 is done by the owner. powershell.exe 5.1.26100.9444 Desktop imports Pester 6.2.0 from C:\Program Files\WindowsPowerShell\Modules\Pester\6.2.0 (12:48:10Z); the Pester 6.x manifests declare PowerShellVersion '5.1'.
   6b. Playwright chromium is provisioned in task 25.
   6c. SQL Server Developer edition service: not provisioned. The service-provider scenario is reported unqualified on this host.
7. Approved: delete the pre-existing residue (task 27).
8. Commit always, then try to push at every checkpoint and ignore a failure (task 1 protocol).
9. Compact advertised MCP tool schemas.
   - tools/list measured 3,294,701 bytes for 12 tools (2026-10-03 12:45:22Z).
   - Deep content is advertised as opaque objects pointing at loom:// schema resources, with full validation server-side and in smoke, and a per-tool size budget (task 29).
10. A field that becomes required on an existing record type lands with the change that supplies it for every existing instance; until then the contract task authors it as optional.
   - LoomConfig: task 5 authors modelId, modelKind and composition (members, delegated roots, output claims) as optional properties. Task 14 makes modelId and modelKind required in the same change as declaration-driven initialize and every fixture and test helper that writes a loom.json.
   - CapabilityRegister: task 8 authors owner, positive and negative tests, proof limits, required environments and evidence reference as optional. Task 26 makes coverage --check enforce them in the same change that fills every entry.
   - Each such change is listed in its task's CHANGED report under the contract-change rule.
   - Reason: requiring a field before anything can supply it breaks the build. The fixed `loom init` scaffold (init.ts:17-25) has no model id or kind to write, and 124 capability entries lack the new fields. That would go against "every commit builds" and "a replaced shape lands with the code that switches to it" (task 1). Inventing defaults is excluded because the spec forbids fabricating missing values.
   - New fields on a record whose every instance the same task can update (Unknown.evidenceNeeded and recommendedAction in task 5, the decision-4 model fields in task 7) are required at once.
11. A multi-action agent tool (loom.workspace, loom.federation, loom.qualify) advertises one output schema whose `data` is an opaque object. Its description names each action's data definition resource (loom://schema/<Data>). The server and smoke validate each action's data against its full definition.
   - Reason: an MCP tool has exactly one outputSchema. Advertising every action's compact data together measured up to 7,938 of the 8,192-byte budget (loom.workspace with open's data), leaving no headroom. An opaque data member keeps the full validation guarantee (task 29) at a fraction of the size. Implemented in task 21.
12. RunRecord takes the spec's run-result member names (2026-10-04, task 8).
   - `id` becomes `runId` and `aggregate` becomes `testOutcome`. The one producer (packages/qualification/src/run.ts:206-218) and every consumer (cli commands.ts:428-510, cli selftest.ts:79-81, the qualification and cli tests, and any document that names the member) switch in the same commit.
   - Reason: the spec's run result names `runId` and `testOutcome`, and QualifyRun already uses `runId`. Keeping `aggregate` beside a new `testOutcome` would give one fact two homes. Renaming within format 1 is allowed because 1.0.0 is the initial release and no released instance exists.
13. Run cleanup has one vocabulary, the spec's (2026-10-04, task 8).
   - The cleanup state is pending|running|clean|failed. It replaces task 6's QualifyRunStatus.cleanup enum pending|complete|residual.
   - QualifyCancelData.cleanup takes the run-cleanup record (state, database/file/process/service outcomes, attempted actions, residual resource identities, recovery reference) instead of CleanupReport.
   - CleanupReport stays the outcome of closing a workspace handle, whose steps (cancel runs, detach watchers, revoke browser access, release the handle) are a different lifecycle.
   - Reason: the spec defines the run's cleanup state and the status operation returns "cleanup status". The task-6 shapes have no producer yet (loom.qualify lands in task 37), so no code switches.
14. The browser host's request and rejection shapes belong to the contract baseline (2026-10-04, task 9; raised by the contract author).
   - The contract had no shape for the bootstrap exchange (POST /api/session: one-use capability in; permitted workspace handles out), the action request (POST …/actions: typed catalogue action plus revision expectations), or a browser rejection. Task 9 authors them in tools.schema.json: BootstrapCapability, BrowserSessionRequest, BrowserSession, BrowserActionRequest and BrowserRejection.
   - An action's result is the same envelope as the agent and CLI action. An action the handle's access does not permit (read access mutating, publishing, running checks or touching policy; edit access attempting acceptance) is the typed refusal `access-denied`, a new RefusalCause, because no existing cause meant that. The MCP read handle and the browser share it.
   - Host, Origin, cookie, bootstrap expiry, one-time use and rate limiting are checked before any operation runs, so their failures are a typed BrowserRejection body rather than a result envelope; no operation ran to produce one. Its unknown-handle cause reuses RefusalCause.
   - Reason: the spec's local HTTP interface table and its browser-security scenario define these exchanges. Contracts precede adapter and client implementations, and completed boundaries must not be redesigned while another component is built. Leaving the shapes to task 23 would have changed the boundary after its baseline.
15. The initialize orientation budget has one home: `mcp.instructionsBudget` in packages/core/schema/operations.json, beside `mcp.toolBudget`, at 2,400 UTF-8 bytes (2026-10-04, task 9; raised by the contract author).
   - Generated as MCP_INSTRUCTIONS_BUDGET. Tasks 10 and 21 read it, and task 21's smoke check holds the instructions to it. Tools/loom/CLAUDE.md gains its single-home row.
   - Reason: the spec limits initialization orientation to 2,400 UTF-8 bytes, and a number with no contract home gets copied into code and tests, where the copies drift.
16. A browser action request is {operation, arguments}; its revision expectations travel inside the arguments, as the operation's own input defines them (2026-10-04, task 9; refines 14).
   - `expectedVector` stays in FederationInput. The single-workspace write's MutationExpectation goes into MutateInput, which task 14 switches.
   - Reason: a second copy on the browser request gave one fact two homes, plus a mismatch rule to police them. The agent tools, the CLI and the browser now share one home for each expectation.
17. Proof limits have one home in the operation catalogue, with the operations they apply to (2026-10-04, before task 10).
   - The four core limits hard-coded in packages/core/src/describe.ts:14-19 move into operations.json as entries {id, text, operations}.
   - Profile proof limits stay in each profile. They apply to the operations the catalogue marks as depending on profiles (projection, check and qualification).
   - describe with an operation returns only the limits relevant to it, deduplicated; without one, it returns none in the summary and the full deduplicated set in a full page.
   - Reason: the spec requires deduplicated proof limits relevant to the requested operation. Nothing mapped a limit to an operation, and a mapping kept in code would be a second, unchecked home beside the catalogue.
18. Guidance text is hand-authored Markdown under Docs/guides/ and embedded into core by the generator (2026-10-04, before task 10).
   - Docs/guides/orientation.md (at most MCP_INSTRUCTIONS_BUDGET bytes, enforced by generate), engineering.md and workflow.md are hand-authored. generate.mjs embeds each with its content digest into src/generated, and generate --check reports drift. loom://guide/capabilities is generated from the catalogue and profiles, not hand-written.
   - Reason: hand-authored guidance owns reasons, decision procedure and examples, while generated records own exact fields and callable signatures. Docs/ is Loom's documentation home, which docs --check --self holds to the release wording, and core stays pure because it reads only generated data.
19. Describe paging is flat on DescribeInput: `detail`, `sections`, `operation`, `cursor` and `budget` are its own members, and DescribePage is removed (2026-10-05, task 10; a demonstrated defect in task 6's contract).
   - Defect: the spec puts `detail: "summary"` (the default) and `detail: "full"` directly on loom.describe, and requires a client-advertised schema to keep the client-supported shape. Under decision 9 a nested object is advertised as an opaque object, so task 6's DescribePage member hid `detail`, `cursor` and `budget` from agents.
   - Impact: owner packages/core/schema/tools.schema.json (DescribeInput changed; DescribePage and its describe-page fixture removed). Consumers: packages/core/src/describe.ts:112 and tools.ts:57-60, packages/cli/src/commands.ts:562-563; the designer reads none of them. Generated: src/generated types, contracts, digest and operations, and Docs/operations.md. Evidence invalidated: task 6's contract and fixture results for DescribePage. CONTRACT_DIGEST moves from the task-9 baseline sha256:e49a6e80… to sha256:ca166683f256ef3f9777701c9326262cedbfefe328049498581d33c4d4c90b7d, together with decision 20 and task 10's catalogue changes. No released instance exists, because 1.0.0 is the initial release.
   - Acceptance: the owner's resume authorization of 2026-10-04 delegates the contract decisions that the spec and the accepted decisions settle; the spec settles this one.
20. A refusal carries its remedies in Refusal.nextActions, an optional list of NextAction (2026-10-05, task 10; a demonstrated defect: a missing shape in task 6's contract).
   - Defect: the spec requires a stale write or continuation to be refused with the current revisions and a re-plan action, and loom.mutate on an imported record to return the owner and a valid next action. The contract had no member that carries an action on a refusal. The current revisions already travel in every envelope's `revisions`, refused results included (result.schema.json ResultEnvelope).
   - Why on Refusal: a refusal is the same record for every tool, so its remedy has one home there; carrying it in each tool's `data` would give one fact a home per tool. WorkspaceSummary.nextActions and the resume context's nextActions carry the next step of the work, a different fact; all three use the one NextAction shape, whose arguments validate against the named tool.
   - Impact: owner packages/core/schema/result.schema.json Refusal (one optional member added; refusal.json fixture with valid and invalid cases). Producers: packages/core/src/envelope.ts:95, used by describe.ts:137 and tools.ts:63 for a stale describe cursor and by the context continuation refusals. Consumers: packages/cli/src/render.ts:26; asserted in packages/mcp-server/src/smoke.ts:168, mcp.test.ts:245, cli.test.ts:476 and core selftest/discovery.ts. Generated artifacts and digest: as decision 19.
   - Acceptance: as decision 19.
21. A workspace's import pins have one home: a pure core function that returns the exact ContractPins the workspace consumes, in canonical order (2026-10-05, before task 14).
   - Until composition resolution switches PublishedContractRef to ContractPin (tasks 11 or 15, per task 5), the function returns the export pins of LoomConfig.composition.members, because a composition consumes its members' exports; a workspace without a composition has none. Tasks 11 and 15 extend the same function; no shape changes.
   - MutationExpectation.imports is the canonical hash of that list, and a single workspace's RevisionVector entry carries the list as its `imports`. The entry's `contract` is CONTRACT_DIGEST and its `generator` is the canonical hash of the generator identity {version: ENGINE_VERSION, contractDigest: CONTRACT_DIGEST} that baselines and the output manifest already record (packages/workspace/src/records.ts:81, outputs.ts:155).
   - Reason: the spec's composition references pinned member exports and published contracts. A ContractPin requires sourceCommit, which PublishedContractRef lacks and PublishedContract.sourceCommit leaves optional, so forming pins from published references now would invent a commit. A published reference loses no identity meanwhile: it sits in the model document with its digest, so the model hash binds it, and the vendored bundle is bound by that digest (packages/workspace/src/published.ts:20-43).
22. Every workspace result reports the hash a caller needs for MutationExpectation.imports in RevisionSet.imports, an optional member (2026-10-05, before task 14; a demonstrated defect: a missing member).
   - Defect: decision 1 and the spec require a single-workspace write to carry the model, config, policy and imports hashes, and RevisionSet exposed the first three but no imports hash, so a caller could not build a valid expectation from any result.
   - A caller's expectation is {model: revisions.model, config: revisions.config.hash, policy: revisions.policy.hash, or null when there is no policy, imports: revisions.imports}. MutateInput replaces `expectedRevision` with a required `expectation` for a workspace mutation (decision 16); the CLI's `mutate --expected <revision>` becomes `--expected-model`, `--expected-config`, `--expected-policy` (a hash, or `none`) and `--expected-imports`. checkRevision, the model-only check of the designer's offline save (apps/designer/src/app/loom-store.ts:384), is a different protocol and stays.
   - A stale write is refused with cause stale-base, a finding naming each input that changed, the current revisions in the envelope, and a Refusal.nextActions entry that re-plans: loom.planChange with { workspace: true }, the current model revision as baseRevision and the refused request's patch or patches and acknowledgeBreaking, which satisfies PlanChangeInput.
   - Impact: owner result.schema.json RevisionSet (one optional member) and tools.schema.json MutateInput; producers: the workspace adapter's result stamping; consumers: the CLI mutate command, the MCP loom.mutate tool, their tests and smoke, the catalogue's mutate usage and examples, Docs/workflow-integration.md §Expected-revision protocol and the README. Acceptance: as decision 19.
23. Initialization records its recovery journal as an InstallJournal at .loom/cache/init-journal.json (2026-10-05, before task 14).
   - The scaffold is staged in a `.loom-staging-*` directory beside .loom and renamed into place, as init does today (packages/workspace/src/init.ts:102-120). The journal is the staging directory's first file, state 'staged' with every entry pending and previousHash null; after the rename it is rewritten 'complete' with every entry installed. Its `bundle` is the canonical hash of the scaffold's writes without the journal, so the dry run knows the final journal's hash. WorkspaceInitializeData.writes lists the journal with role 'journal'.
   - A `.loom-staging-*` directory whose journal is not complete is an interrupted initialization. Initialize reports it as INIT_REPAIR_REQUIRED and, on apply, removes it only when every file in it still has its journal hash; any other content is another writer's and is left in place.
   - InstallJournal's description and its `bundle` description widen from a bundle of generated artifacts to any installed file set, a workspace scaffold included; that is a contract change listed in task 14's report.
   - Reason: the spec requires an atomic scaffold with a recovery journal; reusing the one journal shape keeps one recovery vocabulary, and .loom/cache is ignored by the scaffold's own .gitignore, so the journal is retained without being tracked.
24. The initialization lock lives in the repository's Git directory, as loom-init.lock, resolving a `gitdir:` file for a worktree or submodule (2026-10-05, before task 14).
   - Reason: no .loom exists yet to hold it, and a lock in the working tree would appear as an untracked file and dirty the inspection. The lock touches no index, ref or gitlink. Its holder is a ProcessIdentity {pid, createdAt}; a holder whose pid runs with another creation time is a different process and its lock is taken over, while a creation time that cannot be read keeps the lock held.
25. Each unresolved workspace condition the spec names has its own finding code (2026-10-05, before task 14).
   - CHECKOUT_MISSING: a declared submodule or member repository has no checkout. DESCRIPTOR_UNREADABLE: a .loom/loom.json cannot be read or parsed. ROOT_INACCESSIBLE: the path lies outside the server's allowed roots or cannot be read. An ownership conflict stays SCOPE_OVERLAP.
   - They replace SCOPE_UNRESOLVED wherever it stood for one of these causes (packages/workspace/src/discover.ts:128 and :327, init.ts:61). SCOPE_UNRESOLVED stays only for a cause none of them names, and leaves FindingCode if no use remains.
   - A path outside the allowed roots is refused with cause access-denied, whose description widens to name it; an unreadable path is refused unresolved-context. Inspection itself never refuses for these: it reports ownership status 'unresolved' with the specific finding.
   - Reason: the spec requires a specific unresolved result for a missing checkout, an unreadable descriptor, an inaccessible root and an ownership conflict, and one code per condition lets a caller act without parsing a message.
26. The server's startup directory or `--workspace` value is a discovery hint only (2026-10-05, before task 21).
   - The server offers it as the `path` argument of the loom.workspace inspect and open next actions it returns where a request names no handle: the describe summary's discovery entry and the unknown-handle and unresolved-context refusals. It never selects or opens a workspace, and no call changes it.
   - Reason: the spec limits the startup value to the default discovery hint and forbids a global selection another call can change; the presence rules workspace-inspect and workspace-open require `path`, so the hint can be offered but never applied.
27. The read-only rule for imported records has one home, in core, implemented with composition resolution in task 11 (2026-10-05, before task 21).
   - Task 21 transports every refusal's Refusal.nextActions unchanged and its smoke validates each next action's arguments against the named tool's input; it adds no imported-record logic. Statement #225 is owned by tasks 11 and 21, and #223 gained task 11 as co-owner in the crosswalk (task 21 resolves through the adapter what it resolves today, vendored published contracts; task 11 extends that closure across members).
   - Reason: the rule is a core semantic rule, so a server-side copy would be a second home, and composition imports do not exist before task 11.
28. A write target that no longer resolves inside its workspace immediately before the write is one condition with one result (2026-10-05, task 14; raised by the round-3 worker; a demonstrated defect: one condition with two codes, one of them misused).
   - The finding is WRITE_OUTSIDE_WORKSPACE, rule "A write target still resolves inside its workspace immediately before the write". writeModel, writeState and the output install's write-time and rename-time re-checks raise it, each with refusal cause policy-failure. The writeModel and installOutputs entries of icd/workspace.json already list policy-failure.
   - OUTPUT_OUTSIDE_WORKSPACE stays the planning finding for a declared output route that leaves the workspace. ROOT_INACCESSIBLE and access-denied keep the meanings of decisions 25 and 14 (the server's allowed roots; handle access and capabilities) and are not used for a write target.
   - Defect: packages/workspace/src/write.ts raised ROOT_INACCESSIBLE with access-denied for a link-redirected model or state target. ROOT_INACCESSIBLE's rule (packages/core/src/codes.ts) concerns the allowed roots before inspection or opening, and access-denied (result.schema.json RefusalCause) covers handle access, capabilities, allowed roots and acceptance; a target inside the allowed roots that a link moved is none of these.
   - Reason: the spec requires the containment re-check immediately before a write (loomrefinements.md:115) and names no code. One code per condition lets a caller act without parsing a message (decision 25), and keeping the planning finding separate from the write-time finding distinguishes "the declared route leaves the workspace" from "a link changed after planning".
   - Impact: FindingCode (result.schema.json) and FINDING_RULES (codes.ts) gain one code, with RAISED_ELSEWHERE naming the workspace adapter, a contract change listed in task 14's report; write.ts, outputs.ts and their tests switch; icd/workspace.json gains a writeState entry, which it lacks today. Applied in round 4a (contract digest sha256:d232ff54…).
29. Inspection reports everything the spec lists for it, in WorkspaceInspectData (2026-10-05, task 14; raised by the round-4a worker; a demonstrated defect: missing members in task 6's contract).
   - Defect: loomrefinements.md:119 requires inspection to report the target repository, enclosing composition, existing models, code ownership, direct submodules, missing checkouts, affected tracked and untracked paths and any conflicting claims. WorkspaceInspectData (tools.schema.json) carries only path, repository, ownership, placements and inspectionDigest, so the rest had nowhere to go.
   - Added members, each required because inspection always establishes them:
     - `composition`: the enclosing composition, {descriptor (its .loom directory, relative to the inspection boundary), modelId, listed (whether the target repository is one of its members)}, or null when none encloses the path.
     - `models`: the existing models of the target repository and of its direct submodules, each {descriptor (relative to the repository root), readable, and modelId and modelKind when readable}.
     - `submodules`: the direct submodules .gitmodules declares, each {path, checkedOut, hasDescriptor}. A missing checkout is checkedOut false and is also reported as CHECKOUT_MISSING; "missing checkouts" has this one home.
     - `affectedPaths`: {tracked, untracked}, the paths under the inspected path that Git tracks and that Git reports untracked and not ignored. They are read from Git's index and status for the inspected pathspec only, and each list is bounded by the discovery budget's item limit, with its omissions in the envelope's completeness.
   - Conflicting claims stay in `ownership` (status 'overlap' with each claiming candidate), their one home.
   - WorkspaceHandle.parent, "the composition this workspace is a direct member of", is the same enclosing composition when `listed` is true; open sets it.
   - Reason: the spec names each item, and none had a home; bounding the path lists keeps inspection within the bounded-discovery rules, and Git's pathspec-limited index and status reads keep it from traversing unrelated trees.
   - Impact: tools.schema.json WorkspaceInspectData with its fixture (valid and invalid cases), the workspaceInspect example in operations.json, Docs/operations.md, and the adapter's inspect and open; no consumer exists yet (task 21 exposes them). Acceptance: as decision 19.
30. Inspecting a path that does not exist (2026-10-05, task 14; raised by the round-4a worker).
   - A path inside a declared submodule or composition member whose checkout is missing reports ownership 'unresolved' with CHECKOUT_MISSING and is never refused. Any other path that does not exist is refused invalid-input, as the catalogue's workspaceInspect refusal states.
   - workspaceOpen's catalogue refusals gain access-denied for a path outside the allowed roots, which decision 25 already defines and the catalogue omitted.
   - Reason: OwnershipResult (workspace.schema.json) allows 'ungoverned' only after complete negative resolution, so reporting a path that does not exist as ungoverned asserts an absence nothing measured; and decision 25 requires a missing checkout to be reported rather than refused.

metadata.decision31: 31. Commit everything, and keep the job folder in Loom (owner, 2026-10-05: "Please do commit !", "Please commit all progress made, maybe even copy the Job folder C:\Users\nnbfdh8\.claude\jobs\8058984e\ to the Repo / submodule", and on where: "Commit it to Tools/loom/.claude in the main branch"). When the final task-14 worker reports: task 14 is committed through the ledger if its 13 checks pass, otherwise committed as it stands with the failing check named in the message and recorded with `ledger adopt`; then .claude joins SKIP_DIRS in packages/cli/src/docs.ts (agent configuration is not Loom's own text, and the release-wording gate would otherwise fail on the job files' task numbers, decision numbers and spec labels), with a test; then the job folder, without scratch (task-backup/, progress.cjs), is copied to Tools/loom/.claude/jobs/8058984e/, committed on main, pushed, adopted in the ledger, and the superproject pointer advanced; then the ledger is paused and work stops until the owner asks. This supersedes, for the job folder only, the task 1 protocol rule that the crosswalk stays outside the repository and that spec labels never appear in Loom's tree; the job files also carry user-profile paths, accepted by the owner's choice.
